newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FOCUS - Philippine shares sink to 13-month low.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Philippine shares sink to 13-month low.

text.p: Philippine shares skidded to a 13-month low on Monday after selling hit index leaders but analysts said they hoped the market had plumbed the depths and was ripe for a technical bounce.
"Hopefully, the market will hold its level and we might a see a technical rebound tomorrow," Cilette Liboro, vice president of Orion-Squire Capital Inc said.
The key index of 30 blue chip companies sank in late trade to 2,834.14 points, its lowest in more than a year, but recovered slightly at the bell to close 1.22 percent down at 2,837.31.
It was the lowest the index had fallen to since March 27 last year when it plummetted to 2,834.4 points.
All sub-sectors closed lower. A total of 3.4 billion shares valued at 2.3 billion pesos changed hands in modest trading.
The market, battered since the start of the month by rumours of a property crash, was dragged down further by a lower than expected first quarter performance by Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co.

The country's dominant telecommunations firm announced before trading opened that its unaudited profits for the first quarter had dipped 1.8 percent to 1.28 billion pesos ($48.67 million) because of the cost of a staff redundancy programme.
PLDT closed 10 pesos lower at 1,545 pesos.
The most heavily traded issue, Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co, finished five pesos down at 595 pesos.
Not even the listing of Boulevard Properties BHI PS could bring cheer. It made its debut at 90 centavos, down from its offer price of one peso, and closed even lower at 81 centavos.
"The market is very irrational at this point any bad news they take at face value," Liboro said. "I hope it's the bottom."
Foreign selling also helped further depress the market.
"By my experience, we might have a technical rebound," Leila Calderon, senior investment analyst of Asian Capital Equitie Inc said of prospects for Tuesday.

Philippine Asia Equity Securities Inc said it expected the market to remain depressed all week. "With no fresh news, expect the negative trend to prevail this week," it said in a report. Conversion ($1=26.3 pesos)
